_README: Calibration battery for the cite instrument.
MOS discipline rule 3: every instrument passes its full battery at ONE
shared parameter setting, or it is not used. For a citation resolver the
battery is three classes, analogous to partition / cover / structure-free:
gold     real papers, correctly remembered   -> must reach VERIFIED
nearmiss real papers, garbled by the model   -> must reach PARTIAL/AMBIGUOUS
decoy    papers that do not exist            -> must reach UNRESOLVED
The decoy class is the positive control that Tier 0 kept discovering it
needed. Without it, an instrument that says VERIFIED to everything scores
EPISTEMIC STATUS OF THIS FILE: the gold entries are [UNVERIFIED SEED] --
written from model knowledge, exactly the thing PRECILLA exists to
distrust. They are NOT authority. The first successful `precilla cite
calibrate --promote` run replaces each seed with the resolved DOI and
flips it to [MEASURED]. Until then, a gold entry that fails is ambiguous
between 'bad fixture' and 'bad resolver' and the report says so.
The decoy entries are [DERIVED]: constructed, so known-false by
construction. They carry no such ambiguity, which is why decoy failures
are the harder failure and are reported first.
